result:
The change would reach the REST module through three callers. `saveLocation` is defined in `openmrs-core`, but the `/ws/rest/v1` resources live in a separate repository, `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. `openmrs-core/webservices` has no matches, so I searched the REST repo directly.

**Direct callers in the REST module, best first:**

1. **`LocationResource1_8.save`** is the generic `/ws/rest/v1/location` create/update path. It calls `Context.getLocationService().saveLocation(location)` and returns the result. I did not check whether `LocationResource1_9` or `2_0` override `save`, so they may inherit this behaviour.
2. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9`** calls `saveLocation(delegate.getLocation())` in two places. The first is in the create/save path (line 101), after it adds the attribute to the location. The second is in `delete` (line 113), which voids the attribute and then saves the parent location. I did not read the signature of the save method, so its start line is approximate.
3. **`LocationController1_9Test`** calls `service.saveLocation` at lines 164, 225 and 242. These are tests of the `/location` controller. They would break if the behaviour changed, but they are not production code.

**Indirect paths through core:**

- `LocationServiceImpl.retireLocation` (line 260) and `unretireLocation` (line 269) call `saveLocation`. The REST `DELETE` with `reason` (retire) and `POST` with `retired: false` (unretire) reach these through the generic resource's `save` and `delete` handling. I confirmed the `shouldRetireALocation` and `shouldUnretireALocation` tests exercise this, but I did not trace the `DelegatingCrudResource` code that routes to them.
- `LocationResource1_8.purge` calls `purgeLocation`, not `saveLocation`, so it is not directly affected.
